title: Prompting ChatGPT like a human: Persona, Context, Mission and tree of thought
summary: Ruben Hassid explains how to prompt ChatGPT by treating it like an intern: give a Persona, Context and Mission, and keep the decisions yourself. He also covers token limits, custom instructions, common mistakes, and how he builds LinkedIn content with AI as a helper rather than a replacement.

principles.text: Prompt an AI like you'd brief a human intern: give context, examples and a clear mission, or expect weak output.
principles.quote: the answer is just as good as the prompt

principles.text: Structure prompts as Persona, then Context, then Mission, and make each as specific as possible.
The biggest prompting mistake is not knowing what you want and expecting the AI to know it for you.
principles.quote: not knowing what you want and expecting the AI to know what you want

principles.text: Use AI to brainstorm options and keep the judgment call yourself (tree of thought): pick one branch, then brainstorm again.
principles.quote: you're not asking Chad GPT to select anything you're like Bren storm and I'm gonna pick it one of the answer

principles.text: Phrase instructions affirmatively (say 'stop asking questions' rather than 'don't ask questions') and call out repeated mistakes until it adapts.
principles.quote: always prefer affirmative sentences so avoid at all costs don't do that prefer stop doing that

principles.text: Manage tokens: keep brainstorming chats concise, or front-load a big prompt when you know exactly what you want; custom instructions sit outside the token limit.
principles.quote: this is out of the tokens limits so yeah whatever how long is the conversation CAD GPT will always remember the custom instruction
